content_html:
I have a program that shares files between my laptop and my phone. It works well, except for apostrophes.

When I type an apostrophe 

'
on my laptop, it becomes 
â€™
on my phone. And when I type 
's
on my phone, it becomes 
痴
on my laptop.

Apparently the phone turns the apostrophe (U+0027) into a right single quote (U+2019), then bungles bytes in the UTF-8 encoding of U+2019 as three Windows-1252 characters. The bytes E28099hex are interpreted as 

â
(E2hex), 
€
(80hex), and 
™
(99hex).

When I type 

's
on my phone, it is encoded as two Windows-1252 characters 92hex and 73hex. Then by the time the text appears on my laptop, the bytes 9273hex are interpreted as a Shift-JIS encoding of the CJK character 
痴
(U+75F4).
